Cotton.source_title: Integrated Pest Management Package for Cotton (2014) - National Centre for Integrated Pest Management / DPPQS / NIPHM, Government of India

pests.name: Leaf hopper / Jassid
pests.symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck sap mainly from the leaf underside and inject salivary toxins; affected leaves curl downward, turn yellow then brown ('hopper burn'), and severe attacks stunt or kill young plants and reduce yield.
pests.cultural_control: Summer deep ploughing; proper crop rotation, avoiding cotton after cotton; seed treatment with imidacloprid 70% WS @ 5-7 g/kg seed or thiamethoxam 30% FS @ 10 g/kg seed; balanced (avoid excess) nitrogen; weed-free field for first 8-9 weeks.
pests.biological_control: Conservation of predators (Chrysoperla carnea, coccinellids, spiders, Geocoris, Anthocorid and Nabid bugs) via maize/sorghum/cowpea border rows; egg parasitoids Gonatocerus spp., Lymaenon empoascae, Anagrus flaveolus, Stethynium triclavatum.
pests.chemical_control: Acetamiprid 20% SP; Imidacloprid 17.8% SL; Buprofezin 25% SC; Monocrotophos 36% SL (CIBRC-approved list, Annexure IX)
pests.dosage: Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 10 g a.i./ha (50 g formulation) in 500-600 L water/ha; Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 20-25 ml a.i./ha (100-125 ml formulation) in 500-700 L water/ha; Buprofezin 25% SC @ 250 g a.i./ha (1000 g formulation) in 500-750 L water/ha; Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 175 g a.i./ha (437 ml formulation) in 500-1000 L water/ha

pests.name: Whitefly
pests.symptoms: Direct sap feeding reduces photosynthesis and vigour; honeydew excretion causes sooty mould and lint contamination; leaves curl upward and the insect is the vector of Cotton Leaf Curl Virus.
pests.cultural_control: Avoid growing cotton near citrus orchards; discourage okra near fields; destroy weed hosts (Sida, Abutilon, Ageratum, Convolvulus etc.); avoid excess nitrogen; use yellow sticky traps for mass trapping.
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids Encarsia formosa, Encarsia shafeei, Eretmocerus mundus; predators Dicyphus hesperus, coccinellids, lacewings, Geocoris; entomopathogens Verticillium lecanii and Aspergillus sp.; Verticillium lecanii 1.15% WP formulated.
pests.chemical_control: Acetamiprid 20% SP; Diafenthiuron 50% WP; Spiromesifen 22.9% SC; Triazophos 40% EC; Verticillium lecanii 1.15% WP
pests.dosage: Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 200 g formulation in 500-600 L water/ha; Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 300 g a.i. (600 g formulation) in 500-1000 L water/ha; Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 144 g a.i. (600 ml) in 500 L water/ha; Triazophos 40% EC @ 600-800 g a.i. (1500-2000 ml) in 500-1000 L water/ha; Verticillium lecanii 1.15% WP @ 2.5 kg formulation in 500 L water/ha

pests.name: Thrips
pests.symptoms: Nymphs and adults lacerate leaf tissue and suck cell contents causing silvery/brown necrotic spots, wrinkled and curled leaves, and a rusty field appearance; heavy early infestation delays bud formation.
pests.cultural_control: Same common cultural practices (deep summer ploughing, weed-free field, balanced fertilization); avoid pyrethroid overuse which favours resurgence.
pests.biological_control: Conserve predatory mite Amblyseius swirskii, predatory thrips (Aeolothrips sp.), insidious flower bug (Orius insidiosus); attractant plant French bean.
pests.chemical_control: Buprofezin 25% SC; Fipronil 5% SC; Imidacloprid 17.8% SL; Flonicamid 50% WG
pests.dosage: Buprofezin 25% SC @ 250 g a.i. (1000 g) in 500-750 L water/ha; Fipronil 5% SC @ 75-100 g a.i. (1500-2000 ml) in 500 L water/ha; Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 20-25 ml a.i. (100-125 ml) in 500-700 L water/ha; Flonicamid 50% WG @ 75 g a.i. (100 g) in 500 L water/ha

pests.name: Aphids
pests.symptoms: Phloem feeders causing leaf crumpling and downward curling; honeydew deposits promote sooty mould and stain open bolls (sticky cotton), lowering fibre quality; younger plants suffer more.
pests.cultural_control: Same common cultural practices; conserve natural vegetation/border crops to harbour natural enemies.
pests.biological_control: Parasitoids Aphelinus sp.; predators Chrysoperla carnea, Coccinella septempunctata, Menochilus sexmaculatus, Syrphus spp.
pests.chemical_control: Azadirachtin 0.03% Neem Oil WSP; Acetamiprid 20% SP; Flonicamid 50% WG; Dimethoate 30% EC
pests.dosage: Azadirachtin 0.03% (300 ppm) Neem Oil WSP @ 2500-5000 ml/ha in 500-1000 L water; Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 10 g a.i. (50 g) in 500-600 L water/ha; Flonicamid 50% WG @ 75 g a.i. (100 g) in 500 L water/ha; Dimethoate 30% EC @ 200-300 g a.i. (660 ml) in 500-1000 L water/ha

pests.name: Mirids
pests.scientific_name: Creontiades biseratense Distant (South Zone); Campylomma livida Reuter (Central & North Zone)
pests.symptoms: Feeding on pre-fruiting terminals causes abortion and excessive branching; feeding on squares causes 'blasting' (drying and shedding); feeding on bolls produces sunken black spots and 'parrot beaking' with shrunken, stained seeds.
pests.cultural_control: Common cultural practices; intercropping with maize/sorghum/cowpea to conserve natural enemies; avoid broad-spectrum insecticide use that disrupts predators.
pests.biological_control: Conserve predators such as Geocoris sp., spiders, Chrysoperla carnea and other generalist predators.
pests.chemical_control: General sucking-pest insecticides such as Chlorpyrifos 20% EC or Profenofos 50% EC as per Annexure IX sucking-pest schedule
pests.dosage: Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 250 g a.i. (1250 ml) in 500-1000 L water/ha; Profenofos 50% EC @ 500 g a.i. (1000 ml) in 500-1000 L water/ha (used under general sucking-pest recommendations, no separate CIBRC line specific to mirids in the document)

pests.name: Mealybug
pests.symptoms: Sap feeding with toxic saliva causes distorted, bushy shoots, crinkled/twisted leaves and stunting; attacks stems, branches and bolls, reducing boll size and opening; honeydew leads to sooty mould and severe cases dry the whole plant.
pests.cultural_control: Flooding/ploughing of orchard soil in October-November to expose eggs; raking soil around base; alkathene sheet/grease banding of stem in December; destruction of infested fallen plant parts; avoid moving infested planting material.
pests.biological_control: Parasitoid Aenasius bambawalei, Promuscidea unfasciativentris; predator Cryptolaemus montrouzieri (mealybug destroyer); general zone-specific cultural practices in Annexure VIII.
pests.chemical_control: Verticillium lecanii 1.15% WP; general systemic insecticides (Dimethoate 30% EC, Monocrotophos 36% SL) applied to sucking pests
pests.dosage: Verticillium lecanii 1.15% WP @ 2.5 kg formulation in 500 L water/ha; Dimethoate 30% EC @ 200-300 g a.i. in 500-1000 L water/ha (general sucking pest dose; document emphasizes cultural/biological control as primary strategy for mealybug, per Annexure VIII)

pests.name: Tobacco caterpillar
pests.symptoms: Gregarious larvae skeletonize the leaf undersurface leaving only midrib and veins (papery appearance); also attack flowers, buds and squares causing shedding and feeding holes.
pests.cultural_control: Hand-picking and destruction of egg masses and gregarious larvae; bird perches to encourage predatory birds; light traps and pheromone traps.
pests.biological_control: HaNPV-type NPV, Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki; parasitoids Trichogramma chilonis, Telenomus remus, Chelonus blackburni; predators Chrysoperla carnea, coccinellids, Eocanthecona furcellata.
pests.chemical_control: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC; Novaluron 8.8% SC; Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki
pests.dosage: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 30 g a.i. (150 ml) in 500 L water/ha; Novaluron 8.8% SC @ 100 g a.i. (1000 ml) in 500-1000 L water/ha; Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki, Strain Z-52 @ 750-1000 ml formulation in 500-750 L water/ha

pests.name: Pink bollworm
pests.symptoms: Larvae web flower buds preventing opening ('rosetted bloom'); attack 10-20 day old bolls, feeding on developing seeds; small exit holes on green bolls and stained lint with damaged seeds in open bolls.
pests.cultural_control: Avoid ratooning and extended crop period; destroy crop residues/stalks after harvest; grazing of animals after last picking to reduce carryover; avoid staking stalks near field.
pests.biological_control: Parasitoids Trichogramma achaeae, T. brasiliensis, T. chilotraeae, Apanteles angaleti, Bracon spp.; predatory mite Pyemotes ventricosus.
pests.chemical_control: Carbaryl 50% WP; Cypermethrin 10% EC; Phosalone 35% EC; Fenpropathrin 10%/30% EC
pests.dosage: Carbaryl 50% WP @ 1000 g a.i. (2000 g) in 500-1000 L water/ha; Cypermethrin 10% EC @ 50-70 g a.i. (550-760 ml) in 150-1000 L water/ha; Phosalone 35% EC @ 700 g a.i. (2000 ml) in 500-1000 L water/ha; Fenpropathrin 30% EC @ 75-100 g a.i. (250-340 ml) in 750-1000 L water/ha

pests.name: Spotted and spiny bollworm
pests.scientific_name: Earias vittella Fab. and Earias insulana Boisd.
pests.symptoms: Neonate larvae bore into terminal shoots causing collapse of the apex or 'twining' of the main stem; later, larvae bore into flower buds and bolls with tunnel openings blocked by excrement, causing shedding and premature boll opening.
pests.cultural_control: Common cultural practices; destruction of okra/bhindi crop that carries the pest over between seasons.
pests.biological_control: Parasitoids Bracon greeni, Rogas aligarhensis, Chelonus blackburni; Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki; NPV.
pests.chemical_control: Bacillus thuringiensis Serovar kurstaki 5% WP; Carbaryl 85% WP; Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC
pests.dosage: Bacillus thuringiensis Serovar kurstaki (3a,3b,3c) 5% WP @ 37.5-50 g a.i. (750-1000 g) in 500-1000 L water/ha; Carbaryl 85% WP @ 1200 g a.i. (1411 g) in 500-1000 L water/ha; Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 30 g a.i. (150 ml) in 500 L water/ha

pests.name: Helicoverpa bollworm
pests.symptoms: Larvae feed on leaves initially then bore into squares/bolls/seeds with the head thrust inside; single larva can damage 30-40 fruiting forms; large circular entry holes at boll base and boll rot from secondary infection.
pests.cultural_control: Trap/border crops (marigold, maize, sorghum); handpicking of grown larvae; target younger larval instars with treatments; rotation of chemical groups to manage resistance.
pests.biological_control: HaNPV 0.43% AS @ 2700 ml/ha during early infestation; parasitoids Trichogramma chilonis, Campoletis chlorideae; predators Chrysoperla carnea, Coccinellids, Geocoris sp.
pests.chemical_control: HaNPV 0.43% AS; Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC; Flubendiamide 39.35% SC; Spinosad 45% SC
pests.dosage: HaNPV 0.43% AS @ 2700 ml/ha; Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 30 g a.i. (150 ml) in 500 L water/ha; Flubendiamide 39.35% M/M SC @ 48-60 g a.i. (100-125 ml) in 375-500 L water/ha; Spinosad 45% SC @ 75-100 g a.i. (165-220 ml) in 500 L water/ha

pests.name: Semi-looper
pests.symptoms: Young larvae congregate and feed on leaf lamina causing small punctures; grown larvae feed voraciously leaving only midrib and veins, with black faeces visible on leaves; occasional feeding on tender shoots, buds and bolls.
pests.cultural_control: Common cultural practices; field sanitation and border crops.
pests.biological_control: Fungal pathogen Nomuraea rileyi; predators Chrysoperla carnea, coccinellids.
pests.chemical_control: General lepidopteran-larvae insecticides (Carbaryl 50% WP, Quinalphos) as per bollworm complex schedule
pests.dosage: Carbaryl 50% WP @ 1000 g a.i. (2000 g) in 500-1000 L water/ha; Quinalphos 20% AF @ 350-500 g a.i. (1750-2500 ml) in 750-1000 L water/ha

pests.name: Leaf roller
pests.symptoms: Larvae roll leaf edges inward to the midrib into a trumpet shape fastened with silk and feed inside; severe infestation causes complete defoliation, more pronounced on bottom canopy and field-edge plants.
pests.cultural_control: Common cultural practices; removal and destruction of rolled/folded leaves.
pests.biological_control: General parasitoids and predators of lepidopteran larvae (Chrysoperla carnea, Bracon spp.).
pests.chemical_control: Carbaryl 50% WP (general leaf-feeder schedule, Annexure IX)
pests.dosage: Carbaryl 50% WP @ 1000 g a.i. (2000 g) in 500-1000 L water/ha

pests.name: Red cotton bug
pests.symptoms: Adults and nymphs suck sap from leaves, green bolls and seeds of partially opened bolls, lowering plant vitality; affected bolls open badly with lint stained by excreta, and boll rot follows from secondary bacterial infection.
pests.cultural_control: Common cultural practices; timely destruction of crop residues and volunteer plants that harbour overwintering bugs.
pests.biological_control: Predators Ectomocoris tibialis, Rhynocoris fuscipes, R. kumarii, R. longifrons.
pests.chemical_control: Fluvalinate 25% EC
pests.dosage: Fluvalinate 25% EC @ 50-100 g a.i. (200-400 ml) in 500-1000 L water/ha

pests.name: Dusky cotton bug
pests.symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck sap gregariously from immature seeds which fail to ripen and remain lightweight; discoloration of lint occurs from large numbers of bugs, and crushed bugs during ginning stain and taint the lint.
pests.cultural_control: Common cultural practices; timely picking and removal of crop residues to reduce late-season buildup.
pests.biological_control: Not specifically listed in the document beyond general predator conservation.
pests.chemical_control: General sucking-pest insecticide schedule (as for aphids/jassids) applied late season
pests.dosage: Not separately tabulated in Annexure IX; managed under general sucking-pest chemical recommendations

pests.name: Stem weevil
pests.symptoms: Adult weevil oviposits in a small hole excavated on the stem; grubs tunnel into stems, branches and roots of young seedlings, causing gall-like stem swelling just above ground and wilting of seedlings.
pests.cultural_control: Common cultural practices; destruction of crop residues harbouring grubs/adults.
pests.biological_control: Not specifically listed in the document.
pests.chemical_control: Carbofuran 3% CG; Carbaryl 10% DP
pests.dosage: Carbofuran 3% CG @ 1000 g a.i./ha (33300 g formulation) as soil application; Carbaryl 10% DP @ 25000 g formulation/ha

diseases.name: Bacterial blight / Blackarm / Angular leaf spot
diseases.symptoms: Seed-borne; produces water-soaked spots on cotyledons (seedling blight), angular leaf spot on foliage, vein blight along leaf veins spreading to stem causing sooty black 'black-arm' lesions that can girdle and break the stem; boll lesions also occur. Irrigated crops can lose 5-20% yield.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid dense cropping; use acid-delinted, disease-free seed.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified for this disease in the document.
diseases.chemical_control: Seed treatment with Carboxin + Thiram; foliar streptocyclin (Streptomycin Sulphate + Tetracycline Hydrochloride)
diseases.dosage: Soak seed in 40-50 ppm streptomycin solution before sowing; seed treatment with Carboxin 37.5% + Thiram 37.5% DS @ 3.5 g/kg seed; on first field symptoms spray streptocyclin (Streptomycin Sulphate 90% + Tetracycline Hydrochloride 10% SP) at 25-40 ppm, repeated at 10-15 day intervals (thrice: before flowering, after flowering, 20 days after second spray)

diseases.name: Alternaria leaf spot
diseases.scientific_name: Alternaria macrospora Zimm. / A. alternata (Fr.) Keissler
diseases.symptoms: Spots first appear on seedling cotyledons and enlarge up to 10 mm, coalescing and causing shedding; on green leaves a purple margin surrounds spots, and in humid weather necrotic tissue turns sooty black from sporulation, leading to premature defoliation.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid dense cropping; remove and deep-plough crop residues; destroy alternate weed hosts; use acid-delinted seed; early sowing; wider spacing to reduce humidity build-up.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified for this disease in the document.
diseases.chemical_control: Carbendazim 50% WP
diseases.dosage: On first appearance of disease, spray Carbendazim 50% WP @ 125 g a.i. (250 g formulation) in 750 L water/ha

diseases.name: Myrothecium leaf spot
diseases.symptoms: Circular tan-coloured leaf spots with violet-brown margins surrounded by translucent, concentrically zoned areas bearing black pinhead sporodochia; can also cause pre- and post-emergence damping-off of seedlings, stem lesions, dieback and boll lesions that discolour and embrittle lint.
diseases.cultural_control: Same general leaf-spot cultural measures: field sanitation, deep ploughing of residues, acid-delinted seed, avoid dense cropping.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified for this disease in the document.
diseases.chemical_control: Carbendazim 50% WP (general leaf-spot fungicide schedule, Annexure X)
diseases.dosage: Carbendazim 50% WP @ 125 g a.i. (250 g) in 750 L water/ha on first appearance of leaf spot symptoms

diseases.name: Root rot
diseases.scientific_name: Rhizoctonia solani Kuhn & R. bataticola (Taub.) Butler
diseases.symptoms: Circular patches of affected plants at seedling or later stages; a yellow patch on the lower stem blackens leading to drying; roots discolour, become sticky and secondary roots rot so plants pull out easily; black sclerotia may form beneath the bark.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid fields with a long disease history; deep plough and solarize soil; remove/bury plant debris after harvest; early sowing (April or June rather than May); crop rotation, intercropping with Vigna aconitifolia; green manuring with Sesbania.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified beyond cultural/rotation practices in the document.
diseases.chemical_control: Carboxin 37.5% + Thiram 37.5% DS (seed treatment)
diseases.dosage: Seed treatment with Carboxin 37.5% + Thiram 37.5% DS @ 3.5 g/kg seed

diseases.name: Fusarium wilt
diseases.scientific_name: Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. vasinfectum (Atk.) Snyder & Hansen
diseases.symptoms: Vascular wilt; cotyledons darken along veins with peripheral chlorosis and shed; in older plants, marginal yellowing of lower leaves progresses to chlorotic patches between veins, and under optimal disease conditions all leaves wilt and shed before the stem dries.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid fields with disease history; crop rotation with G. hirsutum or non-host crops; deep ploughing and solarization; use calcium ammonium nitrate instead of ammonium-based N fertilizers; grow resistant varieties (Jayadhar, Vijalpa, Digvijay, Sujaya, G Cot DH7/DH9, Girnar, Daulat, G-22, G-46, Y-1, Sanjay).
diseases.biological_control: Not specified for this disease in the document.
diseases.chemical_control: No specific fungicide listed; management relies on resistant varieties and cultural/rotation practices
diseases.dosage: Not applicable - cultural and host-resistance management only per the document

diseases.name: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus Disease (CLCuD)
diseases.scientific_name: Cotton Leaf Curl Gemini Virus, transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)
diseases.symptoms: Small vein thickening on young upper leaves progressing to upward/downward leaf curling and cup-shaped laminar outgrowths on the leaf underside; severe cases show reduced internodal length, stunting and reduced flowering/fruiting; appears ~45-55 days after sowing, peaking in July.
diseases.cultural_control: Grow resistant hybrids/varieties (H-1117, H-1226, WH-1236, etc. in North India); quarantine measures restricting movement of diseased material; remove alternate weed hosts (Sida, Abutilon, Ageratum, Convolvulus arvensis, etc.); avoid growing near citrus orchards; discourage okra near cotton; destroy volunteer/ratoon plants; avoid excess nitrogen; use yellow sticky traps for whitefly; sow in first fortnight of May to escape peak vector activity.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified beyond vector (whitefly) natural enemy conservation.
diseases.chemical_control: Neem-based formulations, Triazophos 40% EC, Ethion 50% EC (for whitefly vector control)
diseases.dosage: Azadirachtin 0.03% (300 ppm) Neem Oil WSP or Azadirachtin 0.15% W/W Neem Seed Kernel EC @ 2.5-5.0 L/ha; or Triazophos 40% EC @ 1.5 L/ha; or Ethion 50% EC @ 2.0 L/ha, targeting the whitefly vector

diseases.name: Grey mildew
diseases.symptoms: Irregular angular pale translucent leaf spots (1-10 mm, called 'areolae') on lower/older canopy after first boll-set; profuse white sporulation on leaf underside with yellow-green upper leaf discoloration turning necrotic and dark brown; severe cases cause defoliation and premature boll opening with immature lint.
diseases.cultural_control: Remove and deep-plough crop residues; rotate with cereals; grow tolerant varieties (Sujata, Suvin, ERB 4492, SB 289E, Laxmi, Sangam, Varalaxmi) in endemic areas.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified for this disease in the document.
diseases.chemical_control: No fungicide specifically listed for grey mildew in the document
diseases.dosage: Not applicable - cultural/varietal management only per the document

diseases.name: Verticillium wilt
diseases.symptoms: Appears on young plants below 20-24 degC, causing yellowing and drooping of shoots; fruiting-stage plants develop a mosaic pattern on leaves starting at the base, with marginal/interveinal yellowing progressing to red then white necrotic 'tiger stripe' patterning.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid fields with long disease history and ensure good drainage; avoid over-irrigation; use acid-delinted seed.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified for this disease in the document.
diseases.chemical_control: No specific fungicide listed; managed through field selection and cultural practices
diseases.dosage: Not applicable - cultural management only per the document

diseases.name: Leaf rust
diseases.symptoms: Reddish-brown pustules scattered over the leaf surface, more pronounced on older leaves; uredia form small purplish-brown spots that coalesce into large patches; appears in the dry season (December-March) in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat.
diseases.cultural_control: General field sanitation and crop rotation practices as applied to other foliar diseases.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified for this disease in the document.
diseases.chemical_control: No specific fungicide listed for leaf rust in the document
diseases.dosage: Not applicable

Cotton.general_safety_precautions: Basic precautions (Annexure XII) cover: purchase only the required quantity from sealed, labelled containers; store pesticides away from house premises, food/feed, children, livestock, sunlight and rain, and never mix weedicides with other pesticides in storage; never transport pesticides with food; wear hand gloves, face mask and head covering when preparing spray solution using clean water; use correct, non-leaking spray equipment matched to crop stage; avoid tank-mixing multiple insecticides and avoid over-reliance on pyrethroids (max once or twice per season) to prevent sucking-pest resurgence and resistance. Annexure XIII additionally classifies major pesticide groups (organophosphates, carbamates, herbicides) by Insecticides Rules 1971 toxicity class and WHO hazard class, with poisoning symptoms and first-aid/treatment guidance (e.g., atropine and 2-PAM for organophosphate poisoning).
Cotton.waiting_period_notes: The document does not give an explicit numeric pre-harvest interval (PHI)/waiting-period table for cotton pesticides. It instead provides a toxicity/hazard classification and poisoning first-aid annexure (Annexure XIII) and general precaution guidance (Annexure XII), and stresses avoiding repeated/tank-mixed pyrethroid or insecticide applications.

Wheat.source_title: AESA Based IPM Package for Wheat - Directorate of Plant Protection Quarantine and Storage / National Institute of Plant Health Management (NIPHM), Government of India

pests.name: Termites
pests.scientific_name: Odontotermis obesus Rambur, Microtermes obesi Holmgren
pests.symptoms: Feed on roots and stems of growing plants and dead cellulose tissue soon after sowing and near maturity; damaged plants dry up completely and are easily pulled out; later-stage damage produces white, empty ears. Heavier under unirrigated conditions and where undecomposed FYM is applied.
pests.cultural_control: Apply only well-rotten farm yard manure; avoid late sowing; deep summer ploughing (3 ploughings at 10-day intervals); dismantle termite mounds and kill the queen; destroy crop residues that harbour termites; crude oil emulsion in termitaria.
pests.biological_control: Apply neem cake @ 80 kg/acre.
pests.chemical_control: Thiamethoxam 30% FS or Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (seed treatment + soil application)
pests.dosage: Thiamethoxam 30% FS @ 1.32 kg per 40 kg seed; or Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 3-4 ml/kg seed plus 0.8-1.2 L/acre as soil application

pests.name: Wheat aphid
pests.symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck sap particularly from ears, appearing in large numbers during cold, cloudy weather; damage is more severe on heavily manured, well-irrigated, succulent crops which harbour the pest longer.
pests.cultural_control: Regular field monitoring; plant tall barrier crops such as mustard, maize, sorghum or millet around the field.
pests.biological_control: Conserve natural enemies: parasitoids Aphidius spp., Aphelinus spp.; predators syrphid fly, lacewing, minute pirate bug, damsel bug, ladybird beetle, praying mantis, predatory thrips, rove beetle.
pests.chemical_control: Quinalphos 25% EC or Thiamethoxam 25% WG
pests.dosage: Quinalphos 25% EC @ 400 ml in 200-400 L water/acre; or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 20 g in 200 L water/acre

pests.name: American pod borer / Gram pod borer
pests.symptoms: Young larvae feed on leaves initially, then attack earheads, hollowing internal tissues while thrusting the head inside and leaving the body outside; fed leaves, awns and earheads are visible signs.
pests.cultural_control: Growing intercrops (cowpea, onion, maize, coriander, urdbean); guard crop of sorghum/maize around wheat; crop rotation with non-host crops; bird perches to encourage predatory birds.
pests.biological_control: Pheromone traps @ 4-5/acre; inundative release of Trichogramma pretiosum @ 0.4 lakh/acre; conserve parasitoids Tricogramma chilonis, Tetrastichus spp., Chelonus spp., Telenomus spp., Campoletis chloridae, Carcelia spp.; predators spider, dragonfly, coccinellids, lacewing, syrphid flies.
pests.chemical_control: Quinalphos 25% EC
pests.dosage: Quinalphos 25% EC @ 640 ml in 200-400 L water/acre

pests.name: Brown mite
pests.symptoms: Mites suck sap by inserting stylets into leaves; affected leaves become whitish and, under severe conditions, reddish-brown and bronzy; leaves wither and dry.
pests.cultural_control: Use the tolerant variety C-306.
pests.biological_control: Neem oil (2%) or NSKE (5%); conserve predators Oligota spp., green lacewings, predatory mites (Amblyseius alstoniae, Phytoseiulus persimilis), predatory coccinellid Stethorus punctillum.
pests.chemical_control: Quinalphos 25% EC
pests.dosage: Quinalphos 25% EC @ 640 ml in 200-400 L water/acre

pests.name: Pink stem borer / leaf-eating caterpillar
pests.symptoms: Larvae bore into and feed within the stem/leaves; associated with dead-heart type damage in cereal stems.
pests.cultural_control: Erect bird perches @ 10/acre for predatory birds; other measures same as for aphids.
pests.biological_control: Conserve natural enemies (as for common vegetative-stage pests).
pests.chemical_control: Dichlorvos 76% EC
pests.dosage: Dichlorvos 76% EC @ 112.8-150.4 ml in 200-400 L water/acre

pests.name: Shoot fly
pests.scientific_name: Atherigona naqvii Steyskal and A. oryzae Mall
pests.symptoms: Maggots bore into the shoot of young plants a week after germination to about one month, causing the central shoot to dry up ('dead heart'); infestation can reach 60%; later attack may cause side tillers to form and also be attacked.
pests.cultural_control: Regular field monitoring; barrier crops like mustard around field; tall border crops (maize, sorghum, millet); fish meal traps for monitoring.
pests.biological_control: Not specifically listed beyond common biological practices (conserve natural enemies).
pests.chemical_control: Cypermethrin 10% EC or Phorate 10% CG
pests.dosage: Cypermethrin 10% EC @ 220 ml in 200-320 L water/acre; or Phorate 10% CG @ 7500 g/acre

pests.name: Army worm / Cutworm
pests.symptoms: Primary symptom is defoliation; larvae chew leaves from the edge to the midrib or attack cereal heads; heavy infestations can sever the neck just below the head; feeds during dawn/dusk, avoiding sunlight.
pests.cultural_control: Regular field monitoring; barrier crops like mustard around the field.
pests.biological_control: Pheromone traps @ 4-5/acre (ETL 8-10 moths/day/trap); bird perches @ 10/acre; parasitoids/predators same as for Helicoverpa armigera.
pests.chemical_control: Carbaryl 50% WP; Trichlorfon 5% GR/DUST/50% EC; Dichlorvos 76% EC
pests.dosage: Carbaryl 50% WP @ 800 g in 200 L water/acre; or Trichlorfon 5% GR @ 300 g/acre or Trichlorfon 5% DUST @ 300 g/acre or Trichlorfon 50% EC @ 300 ml/acre; or Dichlorvos 76% EC @ 112.8-150.4 ml in 200-400 L water/acre

pests.name: Wheat thrips
pests.symptoms: Infests the flag-leaf sheath and stem, and can attack leaves, stems and heads; heavy nymph/adult feeding gives affected tissue a silvery coloration.
pests.cultural_control: Follow common cultural and biological control practices (no pest-specific chemical listed).
pests.biological_control: Common biological practices (conserve natural enemies).
pests.chemical_control: Not separately specified in the document beyond common practices
pests.dosage: Not applicable - document refers to common practices only for this regional pest

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.symptoms: White, powdery patches form on the upper surface of leaves, sheath, stem and floral parts; powdery growth later becomes blackish lesions causing drying of leaves and other parts. Favoured by high humidity and 20-21 degC.
diseases.cultural_control: Present varieties largely lack adequate resistance; general sanitation of infected debris.
diseases.chemical_control: Triadimefon 25% WP
diseases.dosage: Triadimefon 25% WP @ 200 g in 300 L water/acre

diseases.name: Loose smut
diseases.symptoms: Seed-borne; infection occurs during flowering via wind-borne spores and remains dormant in the seed; infected heads emerge earlier than normal and appear as a mass of olive-black spores covered by a thin grey membrane which ruptures to a powdery head.
diseases.cultural_control: Soak seed in cold water then expose to hot sun 8am-12noon during summer to kill dormant fungus without fungicide; use resistant/tolerant varieties; uproot plants in the standing crop showing yellowing boot-leaf tips before ear emergence; use disease-free seed fields.
diseases.biological_control: Pseudomonas fluorescens 1.75% WP as seed treatment and foliar spray; neem cake @ 80 kg/acre.
diseases.chemical_control: Benomyl 50% WP; Carbendazim 50% WP; Carboxin 75% WP; Tebuconazole 2% DS; Carboxin 37.5%+Thiram 37.5% DS (all seed treatments)
diseases.dosage: Benomyl 50% WP @ 2 g/kg seed; or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 2 g/kg seed; or Carboxin 75% WP @ 2-2.5 g/kg seed; or Tebuconazole 2% DS @ 0.2 kg/10 kg seed; or Carboxin 37.5% + Thiram 37.5% DS @ 3.0 g/kg seed

diseases.name: Brown rust (leaf rust)
diseases.scientific_name: Puccinia recondita f. sp. tritici Eriks. & Henn
diseases.symptoms: Circular to slightly elliptical pustules mostly on upper leaf blades (occasionally sheaths, glumes, awns) containing orange to orange-brown urediospores; up to 30% yield loss under severe infection at 20-25 degC with free moisture.
diseases.cultural_control: Mixed cropping and crop rotation; avoid excess nitrogen.
diseases.chemical_control: Propiconazole 25% EC; Tebuconazole 25% EC; Mancozeb 75% WP; Zineb 75% WP; Thiophanate Methyl 70% WP
diseases.dosage: Propiconazole 25% EC @ 200 ml in 200 L water/acre; or Tebuconazole 25% EC @ 200 ml in 200 L water/acre; or Thiophanate Methyl 70% WP @ 286 g in 300-400 L water/acre; or Zineb 75% WP @ 6-8 kg in 300-400 L water/acre; or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 6-8 kg in 300 L water/acre

diseases.name: Stripe rust / Yellow rust
diseases.symptoms: Bright yellow to orange-yellow pustules arranged in linear stripes on leaves at early crop stage; teliospores also arranged in long dull-black stripes; can occur on sheaths, necks and glumes. Favoured by 10-20 degC with high humidity.
diseases.cultural_control: Mixed cropping and crop rotation; avoid excess nitrogen (same as leaf/stem rust group).
diseases.chemical_control: Propiconazole 25% EC; Tebuconazole 25% EC; Mancozeb 75% WP; Zineb 75% WP
diseases.dosage: Propiconazole 25% EC @ 200 ml in 200 L water/acre; or Tebuconazole 25% EC @ 200 ml in 200 L water/acre; or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 6-8 kg in 300 L water/acre; or Zineb 75% WP @ 6-8 kg in 300-400 L water/acre

diseases.name: Black (stem) rust
diseases.symptoms: Dark reddish-brown pustules on stem, leaf sheaths and leaf surfaces and spikes; pustules usually separate but coalesce under heavy infection; 'flecks' precede pustule formation and tissue feels rough before rupture. Favoured by moisture and temperature above 20 degC.
diseases.cultural_control: Mixed cropping and crop rotation; avoid excess nitrogen.
diseases.chemical_control: Propiconazole 25% EC; Tebuconazole 25% EC; Mancozeb 75% WP; Zineb 75% WP
diseases.dosage: Propiconazole 25% EC @ 200 ml in 200 L water/acre; or Tebuconazole 25% EC @ 200 ml in 200 L water/acre; or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 6-8 kg in 300 L water/acre

diseases.name: Karnal bunt
diseases.symptoms: Field symptoms are hard to distinguish because incidence of infected kernels per head is low and glume spreading is less extensive than common bunt; symptoms are most readily detected on seed after harvest.
diseases.cultural_control: Effective land leveling and drainage (low-lying areas are more prone); decrease seed rate; increase row spacing; delay sowing; avoid irrigation during awn emergence/end of flowering; balanced N and K to avoid lodging; plastic mulching/solarization; burn stubble; crop rotation with non-host crops.
diseases.chemical_control: Propiconazole 25% EC; Bitertanol 25% WP; Thiram 75% WS
diseases.dosage: Propiconazole 25% EC @ 200 ml in 300 L water/acre; or Bitertanol 25% WP @ 896 g in 300 L water/acre; or Thiram 75% WS @ 10-12 g in 400 ml water/acre

diseases.name: Flag smut
diseases.symptoms: Symptoms seen on stem, culm and leaves from late seedling stage to maturity; seedling infection causes twisting and drooping of leaves followed by withering; grey to greyish-black sori with black powdery spore mass form on leaf blade and sheath. Smut spores remain viable over 10 years in soil.
diseases.cultural_control: Use disease-free seed; crop rotation; avoid infected fields.
diseases.chemical_control: Carboxin 75% WP; Tebuconazole 2% DS; Thiram 75% WS
diseases.dosage: Carboxin 75% WP @ 2-2.5 g/kg seed; or Tebuconazole 2% DS @ 0.2 kg/10 kg seed; or Thiram 75% WS @ 10-12 g in 400 ml water/acre

diseases.name: Hill bunt / Stinking smut
diseases.scientific_name: Tilletia tritici (syn. T. caries) and T. laevis (syn. T. foetida)
diseases.symptoms: Fungus attacks 8-10 day-old seedlings, grows systemically along the shoot tip; at flowering, hyphae concentrate in the inflorescence transforming the ovary into a dark-green smut sorus with chlamydospore masses; diseased plants mature earlier with all spikelets affected.
diseases.cultural_control: Use disease-free seed (pathogen survives in seed as primary inoculum source).
diseases.chemical_control: Carboxin 75% WP; Triadimefon 25% WP
diseases.dosage: Carboxin 75% WP @ 2-2.5 g/kg seed; Triadimefon 25% WP @ 200 g in 300 L water/acre

diseases.name: Leaf blight
diseases.scientific_name: Complex of Alternaria triticina, Bipolaris sorokiniana and Alternaria alternata
diseases.symptoms: Reddish-brown oval spots with a bright yellow margin appear on young seedlings; in severe cases several spots coalesce causing drying of leaves. Favoured by ~25 degC and high relative humidity.
diseases.cultural_control: Use certified/resistant seed, timely sowing and crop rotation; plant tall barrier crop for airborne spread.
diseases.chemical_control: Zineb 75% WP; Thiophanate Methyl 70% WP; Mancozeb 75% WP
diseases.dosage: Zineb 75% WP @ 6-8 kg in 300-400 L water/acre; or Thiophanate Methyl 70% WP @ 286 g in 200 L water/acre; or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 6-8 kg in 300 L water/acre

diseases.name: Foot rot
diseases.scientific_name: Pythium graminicolum Subraman and P. arrhenomanes Drechsler
diseases.symptoms: Mainly affects seedlings and roots; rootlets turn brown; seedlings become pale green with stunted growth; pathogen produces sporangia, zoospores and oospores. Favoured by wet weather and high rainfall.
diseases.cultural_control: Soil-borne; manage via drainage and non-host rotation (general foot rot cultural management).
diseases.chemical_control: No pest-specific fungicide separately listed for foot rot in the crop-stage IPM table
diseases.dosage: Not applicable - not separately tabulated in the document

diseases.name: Head scab / Fusarium head blight (and leaf blotch/snow mold phase)
diseases.symptoms: Leaf blotch: oval to elliptical greyish-green mottled lesions with bleached centres that split/shred. Head scab: tan/light brown lesions on one or more spikelets, dark brown discoloration at the base, orange fungal mass on glumes; grain becomes shriveled, chalky white, sometimes pink-discoloured. Favoured by cool, moist weather.
diseases.cultural_control: Use disease-free seed; crop rotation; residue management to reduce soil-borne inoculum.
diseases.chemical_control: Managed under the loose smut/hill bunt/flag smut chemical schedule where applicable (Carboxin, Tebuconazole, Thiram) - no head-scab-specific fungicide separately dosed
diseases.dosage: Not separately tabulated in the document

diseases.name: Helminthosporium leaf blotch (Spot blotch)
diseases.scientific_name: Cochliobolus sativus (Helminthosporium sativum), syn. Bipolaris sorokiniana
diseases.symptoms: Elongated to oval, dark-brown lesions; centres turn light brown to tan surrounded by an irregular dark-brown ring; primary infections on lower leaves begin as chlorotic flecks that enlarge, coalesce and can kill leaves/sheaths prematurely in severe cases. More prevalent in humid, high-rainfall areas.
diseases.cultural_control: Managed as part of the leaf blight complex: certified/resistant seed, timely sowing, crop rotation.
diseases.chemical_control: Zineb 75% WP; Thiophanate Methyl 70% WP; Mancozeb 75% WP (leaf blight complex schedule)
diseases.dosage: Zineb 75% WP @ 6-8 kg in 300-400 L water/acre; or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 6-8 kg in 300 L water/acre

Wheat.general_safety_precautions: Section XV (Basic Precautions in Pesticides Usage) covers: purchase only required quantities from approved-label, sealed containers with invoice; store away from house premises, food/feed, children and livestock, away from sunlight/rain, and never store weedicides with other pesticides; never transport with food; wear gloves, face mask and head covering while preparing spray solution with clean water, never mixing granules with water or smelling/tasting concentrate; use correct, non-leaky equipment with proper nozzles (never unclog by mouth); do not apply on hot/windy days or just before/after rain; avoid tank-mixing different pesticides; wash equipment after use; dispose of leftover solution away from water sources and crush/bury used containers, never reusing them. Section XIV separately tabulates pesticide toxicity classification (Insecticide Rules 1971 / WHO hazard class), poisoning symptoms and first-aid/antidote guidance (e.g., atropine sulphate for organophosphate poisoning).
Wheat.waiting_period_notes: No explicit numeric pre-harvest waiting-period/PHI table is given for individual pesticides. Section XII (Safety Measures) instead addresses pre-harvest handling (timely harvest to avoid shattering/sprouting/weathering) and post-harvest grain storage safety (keeping grain dry below 12.5% moisture, cool below 10 degC, insect-free); it recommends grain deterioration control via aeration, heat treatment, fumigation and other IPM-based storage pest management rather than specifying pesticide waiting days.

Tomato.source_title: AESA Based IPM Package for Tomato - Directorate of Plant Protection Quarantine and Storage / National Institute of Plant Health Management (NIPHM), Government of India

pests.name: Serpentine leaf miner
pests.symptoms: Apodous maggots mine between the epidermal leaf layers producing serpentine (snake-like) mines; leaves dry and drop in severe cases.
pests.cultural_control: Avoid excess nitrogen use; ecological engineering with beans as intercrop reduces attack; yellow sticky traps/cards @ 10/acre.
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids Tetrastichus ovularum, Gronotoma micromorpha, Diglyphus sp., Opius phaseoli, Chrysocharis pentheus, Neochrysocharis formosa; predators lacewings, lady beetles, spiders, fire ants.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed as chemical control in the crop-stage IPM table (cultural/biological control emphasized); general systemic insecticides used against sucking pests may suppress it
pests.dosage: Not separately tabulated in the document for this pest

pests.name: Gram pod borer
pests.symptoms: Young larvae feed on leaves then attack fruits, hollowing internal tissue with the head thrust inside; produces bored fruits with round holes and fed leaves/shoots/buds.
pests.cultural_control: Ecological engineering with intercrops (cowpea, onion, maize, coriander, urdbean); guard crop of sorghum/maize; repellent plant Ocimum/Basil; marigold as ovipositional trap crop; bird perches @ 20/acre; pheromone traps @ 4-5/acre; light trap @ 1/acre.
pests.biological_control: Inundative release of Trichogramma pretiosum @ 40,000/acre 4-5 times from flower initiation; conserve Tetrastichus spp., Telenomus spp., Campoletis chlorideae; spray azadirachtin or HaNPV 0.43%/2% AS with jaggery; Bacillus thuringiensis var. galleriae; entomopathogenic nematodes (Steinernema feltiae).
pests.chemical_control: Indoxacarb 14.5% SC; Flubendiamide 20% WG; Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC; Lambda-cyhalothrin 4.9% CS
pests.dosage: Indoxacarb 14.5% SC @ 160-200 ml in 120-240 L water/acre; or Flubendiamide 20% WG @ 40 g in 150-200 L water/acre; or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 60 ml in 200 L water/acre; or Lambda-cyhalothrin 4.9% CS @ 120 ml in 200 L water/acre

pests.name: Tobacco caterpillar
pests.symptoms: Gregarious larvae skeletonize leaves and can defoliate the crop; feeds on foliage and fruiting parts causing significant loss when populations are high.
pests.cultural_control: Field sanitation; pheromone traps @ 4-5/acre; light trap @ 1/acre; castor as ovipositional trap crop; bird perches @ 20/acre.
pests.biological_control: Release Trichogramma pretiosum @ 20,000/acre/week x4; spray NSKE 5% or azadirachtin against eggs/first instar; conserve Trichogramma chilonis, Chelonus blackburni, Campoletis chlorideae; entomopathogenic nematodes (Steinernema feltiae) @ 2,50,000 infective juveniles/sq. m.
pests.chemical_control: Trichlorfon 5% GR/DUST; Indoxacarb 14.5% SC; Flubendiamide 20% WG; Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC
pests.dosage: Trichlorfon 5% GR or DUST @ 300 g/acre; or Indoxacarb 14.5% SC @ 160-200 ml in 120-240 L water/acre; or Flubendiamide 20% WG @ 40 g in 150-200 L water/acre; or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 60 ml in 200 L water/acre

pests.name: Whitefly
pests.symptoms: Causes chlorotic spotting, yellowing, downward curling and drying of leaves; the principal vector transmitting Tomato Leaf Curl Virus.
pests.cultural_control: Field sanitation and roguing of affected plants; barrier crops (maize/sorghum); peppermint as a repellent plant; yellow sticky traps/cards @ 10/acre.
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids Encarsia sp., Eretmocerus spp.; predators Dicyphus hesperus, lacewings, ladybirds, big-eyed bugs; spray NSKE 5% or azadirachtin 5% W/W neem extract concentrate @ 80 g in 160 L water/acre.
pests.chemical_control: Dimethoate 30% EC; Imidacloprid 17.8% SL; Thiamethoxam 25% WG; Spiromesifen 22.9% SC
pests.dosage: Dimethoate 30% EC @ 396 ml in 200-400 L water/acre; or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 60-70 ml in 200 L water/acre; or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 80 g in 200 L water/acre; or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 250 ml in 200 L water/acre

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.symptoms: Affected leaves become reddish-brown and bronzy; severe infestation shows silken webbing on leaves; leaves wither and dry, and flower/fruit formation is affected.
pests.cultural_control: Field sanitation and roguing; tall border crops such as maize, sorghum.
pests.biological_control: Conserve predatory mites (Phytoseiulus spp., Amblyseius spp.), staphylinids (Oligota spp.), lady beetles, lacewings, predatory thrips, anthocorid bugs (Orius spp.), mirid bugs, hover flies.
pests.chemical_control: Fenzaquin 10% EC; Spiromesifen 22.9% SC
pests.dosage: Fenzaquin 10% EC @ 500 ml in 200 L water/acre; or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 250 ml in 200 L water/acre

pests.name: Root-knot nematode
pests.symptoms: Infects plant roots causing galling; leads to stunted growth and reduced vigour of nursery/field plants.
pests.cultural_control: Crop rotation with cereal crops; ecological engineering with marigold/mustard as intercrops; raise nursery in nematode-free or solarized beds.
pests.biological_control: Not separately listed beyond cultural rotation and solarization.
pests.chemical_control: Dazomet technical (nursery soil fumigant)
pests.dosage: Dazomet technical @ 12-16 g/acre (nursery application)

pests.name: Aphids (regional pest)
pests.scientific_name: Myzus persicae, Aphis gossypii, Aphis fabae, Aphis craccivora
pests.symptoms: Sap-sucking causing leaf curling and vigour loss; honeydew promotes sooty mould; can transmit viral diseases (regional significance pest).
pests.cultural_control: Install yellow sticky traps @ 4-5/acre; judicious use of nitrogenous fertilizers.
pests.biological_control: Release first-instar green lacewing (Chrysoperla carnea) @ 4000/acre; conserve ladybird beetles (Coccinella septempunctata, Menochilus sexmaculata) and parasitoid Aphidius colemani; spray azadirachtin 5% W/W neem extract @ 80 g in 160 L water/acre.
pests.chemical_control: Dimethoate 30% EC
pests.dosage: Dimethoate 30% EC @ 264 ml in 200-400 L water/acre

diseases.name: Damping off
diseases.symptoms: Pre-emergence phase kills seed/seedling before soil emergence with complete rotting; post-emergence phase infects the collar at ground level causing soft, water-soaked tissue and seedling collapse/toppling.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid excessive watering and poorly drained nursery areas; use raised beds (15 cm) or pro-trays.
diseases.biological_control: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride 1% WP @ 9 g/kg seed.
diseases.chemical_control: Captan 75% WS (seed treatment); Captan 75% WP (soil drench)
diseases.dosage: Seed treatment with Captan 75% WS @ 20-30 g/kg seed; soil drench with Captan 75% WP @ 1000 g in 400 L water/acre

diseases.name: Septoria leaf spot
diseases.symptoms: Small, round to irregular spots with grey centre and dark margin, starting on lower leaves and progressing upward; spots coalesce causing blighting and complete defoliation; stems/flowers occasionally attacked, fruit rarely.
diseases.cultural_control: Removal and destruction of affected plant parts.
diseases.chemical_control: Mancozeb 75% WP
diseases.dosage: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 300 L water/acre

diseases.name: Bacterial stem and fruit canker
diseases.scientific_name: Clavibacter michiganensis subsp. michiganensis (Smith) Davis et al.
diseases.symptoms: White blister-like leaf-margin spots turning brown with age; light-coloured stem/petiole streaks develop cracks and cankers with slimy bacterial ooze in humid weather; small water-soaked, white-haloed fruit spots become raised, tan and rough; vascular discolouration visible in split stems.
diseases.cultural_control: Same as seed/seedling stage measures: disease-free seed beds, sanitation, avoiding overhead contamination.
diseases.chemical_control: Streptomycin sulfate 9% + Tetracycline hydrochloride 1% SP (streptocycline)
diseases.dosage: Spray streptocycline 40-100 ppm after appearance of first true leaves; two sprays - one before transplanting (seed beds) and one after transplanting (main field)

diseases.name: Early blight
diseases.scientific_name: Alternaria solani (Ell. & Mart.), A. alternata, A. alternata f.sp. lycopersici
diseases.symptoms: Small black lesions on older foliage enlarge with concentric 'bull's-eye' rings; surrounding tissue yellows and, under high heat/humidity, much foliage is killed; also infects fruit via calyx/stem attachment with large concentric-ringed lesions.
diseases.cultural_control: Use resistant/tolerant cultivars; change nursery bed location each season; remove weeds/volunteer tomato plants; avoid planting overlapping crops nearby.
diseases.chemical_control: Azoxystrobin 23% SC; Mancozeb 75% WG; Copper oxychloride 50% WP; Captan 75% WP
diseases.dosage: Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 200 ml in 200 L water/acre; or Mancozeb 75% WG @ 400 g in 200 L water/acre; or Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 1000 g in 300-400 L water/acre; or Captan 75% WP @ 666.8 g in 400 L water/acre

diseases.name: Bacterial leaf spot
diseases.symptoms: Small brown water-soaked circular leaf spots with a yellow halo; older-plant leaflet infection mostly on older leaves causing defoliation; green fruit develops small water-soaked spots that raise, enlarge and become scabby; ripe fruit not susceptible.
diseases.cultural_control: Same as seed/seedling stage measures; avoid solanaceous weed hosts (Solanum nigrum).
diseases.chemical_control: Streptomycin sulfate 9% + Tetracycline hydrochloride 1% SP (streptocycline)
diseases.dosage: Spray streptocycline 40-100 ppm solution; two sprays timed as for bacterial canker

diseases.name: Bacterial wilt
diseases.symptoms: Rapid, complete wilting of normally grown plants; lower leaves may drop before wilting; cut infected stems immersed in water show a white bacterial ooze streak from the cut end.
diseases.cultural_control: Crop rotation (cowpea-maize-cabbage, okra-cowpea-maize, finger millet-brinjal etc.); rotate with paddy; use pathogen-free seedlings; restrict irrigation water flow from affected to healthy fields.
diseases.chemical_control: No specific bactericide listed; managed through resistant rotation and sanitation
diseases.dosage: Not applicable - cultural/biological management only per the document

diseases.name: Leaf curl (Tomato leaf curl virus)
diseases.scientific_name: Tomato leaf curl virus (ToLCV), transmitted by whitefly
diseases.symptoms: Severe stunting with downward rolling and crinkling of leaves; newly emerging leaves show slight yellowing then curling; older leaves become leathery and brittle; internodes shorten and plants become pale, bushy and stunted.
diseases.cultural_control: Raise nursery under insect-proof net to exclude whitefly vector; use seed from disease-free plants; rogue infected nursery plants; staking to keep fruit off ground; avoid using infected seedlings for transplanting.
diseases.biological_control: Conserve parasitoids Encarsia sp., Eretmocerus spp.; predators as for whitefly management.
diseases.chemical_control: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (root-dip vector control)
diseases.dosage: Before transplanting, dip seedling roots for 15 minutes in Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 60-70 ml in 200 L water/acre

diseases.name: Mosaic (Tomato Mosaic Virus)
diseases.symptoms: Light and dark green mottling on leaves, sometimes with wilting of young leaves on sunny days at first infection; leaflets distorted, puckered and smaller than normal, sometimes with 'fern leaf' symptoms; plants appear stunted, pale green and spindly.
diseases.cultural_control: Use seed from disease-free healthy plants, rinsed and shade-dried; remove and destroy infected nursery plants; avoid using infected seedlings; rotate away from other solanaceous crops (potato, chilli, capsicum, brinjal, tobacco).
diseases.chemical_control: No chemical control - the virus spreads via contact/tools/hands, so sanitation is the primary measure
diseases.dosage: Not applicable

diseases.name: Tomato spotted wilt disease
diseases.scientific_name: Peanut Bud Necrosis Virus (PBNV) / TSWV group, transmitted by thrips
diseases.symptoms: Stunting, chlorotic/necrotic ring spots on leaves, vein thickening and bronzing of young leaves, die-back of growing tips; ripe fruit shows pale red/yellow areas with concentric circular marking and seed discoloration.
diseases.cultural_control: Managed primarily by controlling thrips vectors (Frankliniella schultzii, Scirtothrips dorsalis) and removing alternate weed/crop hosts.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified in the document beyond general thrips natural-enemy conservation.
diseases.chemical_control: No disease-specific chemical listed; vector (thrips) management is the primary control
diseases.dosage: Not applicable

diseases.name: Fusarium wilt
diseases.scientific_name: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lycopersici (Sacc.) W.C. Snyder and H.N. Hans.
diseases.symptoms: First symptom is clearing of veinlets and leaf chlorosis; younger leaves die in succession and the whole plant may wilt and die within days; petioles droop; later, vascular browning occurs and plants become stunted and die.
diseases.cultural_control: Not separately listed beyond general rotation practices.
diseases.biological_control: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride 1% WP @ 9 g/kg seed; root-zone application of 2.5 kg T. viride 1% WP mixed in 150 kg compost/FYM applied after sowing/transplanting.
diseases.chemical_control: No specific fungicide listed; biological seed/soil treatment is the primary control
diseases.dosage: Not applicable - see biological_control dosage for Trichoderma viride

diseases.name: Buck eye rot / fruit rot (regional)
diseases.symptoms: Fruit rot affecting fruits in contact with or near the soil; part of the regional-significance disease list managed with staking and drainage.
diseases.cultural_control: Use resistant varieties; staking and removal of fruits/leaves touching the ground (up to 30 cm); good soil drainage; periodic clipping of lower leaves and mulching.
diseases.chemical_control: Mancozeb 75% WP; Propineb 70% WP
diseases.dosage: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 300 L water/acre; or Propineb 70% WP @ 120 g in 40 L water/acre

Tomato.general_safety_precautions: The document notes (Section XII, at time of harvest) that the 'waiting period for all the pesticides, if any, should be observed without fail' when picking fruit, alongside careful harvesting practice (twisting rather than pulling fruit, harvesting only when vines/fruit are dry). A separate Safety Parameters section (XIV) and Basic Precautions section (XV) cover pesticide toxicity classification, poisoning symptoms/first aid, and standard purchase/storage/handling/application/disposal precautions (buy only required quantity in sealed labelled containers; store away from food, children and livestock; wear gloves/mask when mixing; avoid tank-mixing; do not spray in high wind or just before/after rain; dispose of containers by crushing and burying away from water sources).
Tomato.waiting_period_notes: The document explicitly instructs that 'waiting period for all the pesticides, if any, should be observed without fail' before harvest, but does not provide a specific numeric PHI table per pesticide active ingredient for tomato; growers are directed to the product label/CIBRC recommendation for the exact waiting period of each pesticide used.

Onion.source_title: AESA Based IPM Package for Onion - Directorate of Plant Protection Quarantine and Storage / National Institute of Plant Health Management (NIPHM), Government of India

pests.name: Onion thrips
pests.symptoms: Adults and larvae feed within the leaf mesophyll with a punch-and-suck motion, removing chlorophyll and leaving white-to-silvery patches/streaks; heavy feeding gives leaves a silvery cast that can wither, with tiny black excrement 'tar' spots visible.
pests.cultural_control: Use resistant/tolerant varieties; field sanitation; avoid successive planting of garlic/preferred hosts (cabbage, cotton, tomato, cucumber, melons, pumpkin, strawberry); plant upwind of already-infested crop; adjust transplanting dates; reflective silver plastic/aluminium-painted mulch; sprinkler irrigation reduces thrips versus drip/surface irrigation; barrier rows of maize/wheat.
pests.biological_control: Conserve parasitoid Ceranisus menes; predators syrphid flies, minute pirate bug (Orius tantilus, Blaptosthethus sp., Buchananiella whitei), praying mantis, predatory thrips (Aeolothrips fasciatum), damsel bug, lacewings, coccinellids (Cheilomenes sexmaculata), spiders.
pests.chemical_control: Dimethoate 30% EC; Oxydemeton methyl 25% EC; Quinalphos 25% EC; Lambda-cyhalothrin 5% EC
pests.dosage: Dimethoate 30% EC @ 264 ml in 200-400 L water/acre; or Oxydemeton methyl 25% EC @ 480 ml in 200-400 L water/acre; or Quinalphos 25% EC @ 480 ml in 200-400 L water/acre; or Lambda-cyhalothrin 5% EC @ 120 ml in 120-160 L water/acre (add spreader/sticker 0.05-1.0%; direct spray to leaf bases)

pests.name: Onion maggot
pests.symptoms: Legless maggots enter at the plant base; damaged seedlings first wilt, become flaccid and die, sometimes before maggots are fully grown; second-generation maggots feeding on developing bulbs cause distorted growth with rotting tissue; third-generation feeding on late bulbs renders them unmarketable.
pests.cultural_control: Avoid close spacing; follow crop rotation; field sanitation.
pests.biological_control: Conserve predators such as ground beetles, rove beetles and spiders by providing grassy refuge strips.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in the document; managed primarily through cultural and biological control
pests.dosage: Not applicable - no chemical dosage tabulated in the document for this pest

pests.name: Bulb mite
pests.symptoms: Infested bulbs may rot and fail to sprout, or produce off-colour, stunted, distorted growth; mites rapidly turn injured bulbs into rotten pulp; infestation generally indicates the bulb was already injured (by other pests, mechanical damage or improper storage).
pests.cultural_control: Avoid planting onion after cole crops (e.g., cauliflower, which can harbour high bulb mite populations); avoid successive onion/garlic crops; flood irrigation reduces soil mite levels.
pests.biological_control: Conserve predators: anthocorid bugs (Orius spp.), mirid bugs, syrphid/hover flies, green lacewings (Mallada basalis, Chrysoperla zastrowi sillemi), predatory mites (Amblyseius spp., Phytoseiulus persimilis), predatory coccinellid (Stethorus punctillum), staphylinid beetle (Oligota spp.), predatory cecidomyiid fly and gall midge, spiders.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in the document; managed through cultural and biological control
pests.dosage: Not applicable

pests.name: Eriophyid mite
pests.symptoms: Adults and immatures feed on young leaves and between bulb scale layers, causing stunting, twisting, curling and discoloration of foliage and scarification/drying of bulb tissue; feeding damage is also linked to transmission of viruses.
pests.cultural_control: Flood irrigation reduces mite level in the soil; avoid successive onion/garlic crops.
pests.biological_control: Conserve the same predator complex as for bulb mite (anthocorid bugs, mirid bugs, syrphid flies, green lacewings, predatory mites, coccinellids, staphylinid beetle, predatory gall midge, spiders).
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in the document
pests.dosage: Not applicable

pests.name: Red spider mite
pests.symptoms: Adults/nymphs feed mainly on leaf undersides, causing stippled dots (feeding punctures) on the upper leaf surface, visible silk webbing, and leaves that eventually bleach, discolour and may fall off.
pests.cultural_control: A thorough water spray washes mites off the plant.
pests.biological_control: Conserve and augment natural enemies: anthocorid bugs, mirid bugs, syrphid/hover flies, green lacewings, predatory mites, coccinellids, staphylinid beetle, predatory gall midge, spiders.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in the document; cultural/biological control emphasized
pests.dosage: Not applicable

pests.name: Gram pod borer / Tobacco caterpillar (regional)
pests.symptoms: Polyphagous lepidopteran larvae feeding on foliage and reproductive parts; regional-significance pests of onion/garlic in Punjab and other states.
pests.cultural_control: Field sanitation; ecological engineering with intercrops (cowpea, maize, coriander, urdbean); guard crop of sorghum/maize; repellent Ocimum/Basil and marigold as trap crop; bird perches @ 20/acre; pheromone traps @ 4-5/acre; light trap @ 1/acre.
pests.biological_control: Inundative release of Trichogramma pretiosum @ 40,000/acre 4-5 times from flower initiation; conserve Tetrastichus spp., Telenomus spp., Campoletis chlorideae; predators Chrysoperla zastrowi sillemi, coccinellids, king crow, mynah, spiders, reduviid bug, Geocoris sp.; entomopathogenic nematodes (Steinernema feltiae) @ 20-120 crore infective juveniles/acre.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in the crop-stage table for onion (biological/cultural emphasis)
pests.dosage: Not applicable - not separately tabulated for onion in the document

diseases.name: Damping off
diseases.scientific_name: Pythium spp., Rhizoctonia solani, Fusarium oxysporum, Sclerotium rolfsii, S. cepivorum, Colletotrichum sp.
diseases.symptoms: Pre-emergence damping off causes seed/seedling rot before emergence; post-emergence damping off attacks the collar region at the soil surface, rotting the collar and collapsing seedlings; causes about 60-75% damage in kharif/rainy season under high soil moisture and humidity.
diseases.cultural_control: Soil solarization of nursery beds with clear polythene for 30 days before sowing; avoid continuous nursery use on the same plot; avoid excess soil moisture; follow crop rotation; proper drainage/leveling; sow clean healthy seed on raised beds; avoid overcrowding; use well-decomposed FYM.
diseases.biological_control: Not specifically listed beyond general Trichoderma/Pseudomonas fluorescens seed and soil treatment recommended across pre-sowing stage.
diseases.chemical_control: No pest-specific fungicide dosage listed for onion damping off in the crop-stage table
diseases.dosage: Not applicable - relies on cultural control per the document

diseases.name: Purple blotch
diseases.symptoms: Small, sunken, whitish flecks with purple-coloured centres on leaves and flower stalks; lesions may girdle leaves/stalks causing drooping, and infected plants fail to develop bulbs. Favoured by hot, humid climate (21-30 degC, 80-90% RH).
diseases.cultural_control: Use healthy seed; crop rotation 2-3 years with non-host crops; proper drainage; recommended N and P doses; hot-water seed soaking (50 degC for 20 minutes); use resistant varieties.
diseases.chemical_control: Difenoconazole 25% EC; Kitazin 48% EC
diseases.dosage: Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 40 ml in 200 L water/acre; or Kitazin 48% EC @ 80 ml in 80 L water/acre

diseases.name: Stemphylium leaf blight
diseases.symptoms: Infects radical leaves of transplanted seedlings at the 3-4 leaf stage (late March/early April); small yellowish-to-orange flecks/streaks develop into elongated spindle-shaped spots with pinkish margins; severe on inflorescence stalks of seed crops. Favoured by warm (18-25 degC), humid conditions with long leaf wetness (16+ hours).
diseases.cultural_control: Field sanitation - collect and burn crop residues; long rotation with non-host crops; proper field drainage and reduced plant density; hot-water seed soaking (50 degC, 20 min); plant resistant/moderately resistant varieties (Welsh onion lines).
diseases.chemical_control: Mancozeb 75% WP; Zineb 75% WP
diseases.dosage: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 300 L water/acre; or Zineb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 300-400 L water/acre

diseases.name: Colletotrichum blight / Anthracnose / Twister disease
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked pale yellow spots initially on leaves spread lengthwise covering the whole blade; affected leaves shrivel and droop down (twisted/curled). Most severe in warm (25-30 degC), moist, organic-matter-rich soils; growth slows sharply below 15 degC.
diseases.cultural_control: Field sanitation - destruction of infected plant debris; use resistant varieties.
diseases.chemical_control: No chemical control listed in the crop-stage table; cultural sanitation is the primary measure
diseases.dosage: Not applicable

diseases.name: Onion yellow dwarf disease
diseases.scientific_name: Onion yellow dwarf virus, transmitted by aphids
diseases.symptoms: First symptoms are yellow streaks at the bases of the first true leaves of young onions; all subsequently developed leaves show yellow streaking to complete yellowing; leaves sometimes crinkled and flattened, and bulbs are undersized.
diseases.cultural_control: Manage the aphid vector population; plant virus-free transplants; crop rotation of at least 3 years; remove and destroy diseased plants; rogueing and isolation from susceptible/volunteer crops; use blue sticky traps.
diseases.biological_control: Conserve predators (coccinellids, lacewings, spiders, wasps) that control the aphid vector.
diseases.chemical_control: No disease-specific chemical listed; vector (aphid) management is primary control
diseases.dosage: Not applicable

diseases.name: Iris yellow spot disease
diseases.scientific_name: Iris yellow spot virus, transmitted persistently by onion thrips
diseases.symptoms: Cream-coloured, elliptical/diamond-shaped spots on leaves and on onion flower stalks (scapes); infected leaves and scapes can collapse at the spot site; disease severity correlates with thrips population and can devastate the whole crop.
diseases.cultural_control: Plant healthy seedlings free of thrips and virus; rotate 3+ years between onion crops; eliminate alternate host plants, culls and weeds; use sprinkler irrigation to suppress thrips; avoid thin, patchy stands and crop stress.
diseases.biological_control: As for onion yellow dwarf - conserve predators of the thrips vector (coccinellids, lacewings, spiders, wasps).
diseases.chemical_control: No disease-specific chemical listed; managed via thrips vector control (see Onion thrips chemical control)
diseases.dosage: Not applicable - see Onion thrips entry for vector chemical control

diseases.name: Downy mildew (regional)
diseases.symptoms: Leaves turn pale green; cottony white mycelial growth develops on leaves which gradually turn pale yellow to dark brown and dry up. Favoured by warm, humid climate.
diseases.cultural_control: Select healthy bulbs for seed production; 3-4 year rotation with non-host crop; dispose of infected debris/culled bulb refuse properly; avoid late planting, poor drainage, high fertilizer doses and frequent irrigation; use resistant varieties; expose seed-crop bulbs to sun for 12 days to destroy fungus.
diseases.chemical_control: Zineb 75% WP
diseases.dosage: Zineb 75% WP @ 600-800 g in 300-400 L water/acre

diseases.name: Fusarium basal rot (regional)
diseases.scientific_name: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cepae Schlecht
diseases.symptoms: Initial yellowing of leaves and stunted growth, drying from tip downward; roots turn pink and rot in early stages; in advanced stages the bulb decays from the lower end and the whole plant dies. Favoured by moist soil and ~27 degC.
diseases.cultural_control: 4-5 year rotation with non-host crop; mixed cropping with tobacco/sorghum reduces inoculum; soil solarization (25-gauge polythene, 30 days summer); proper drainage; deep summer ploughing; avoid injury during cultural operations; flood soil in off-season; use resistant varieties.
diseases.chemical_control: No fungicide separately dosed; cultural/soil-management is the primary control
diseases.dosage: Not applicable

diseases.name: White rot / Sclerotial rot (regional)
diseases.symptoms: Initial yellowing and dieback of leaf tips; scales, stem plate and roots are destroyed; bulbs become soft and water-soaked; white fluffy/cottony mycelial growth with abundant mustard-grain-like black sclerotia develops on infected bulbs. Most severe in cool, dry soils.
diseases.cultural_control: Use disease-free areas; rotate with cereal crops; hot-water bulb treatment at 49 degC; soil solarization at 35 degC for 18 hours or 45 degC for 6 hours (reduces disease incidence 50-70%).
diseases.chemical_control: No fungicide separately dosed for white rot
diseases.dosage: Not applicable

diseases.name: Pink root rot (regional)
diseases.symptoms: Reduced bulb size; roots turn pink or maroon when infected; in severe cases roots die and plants become weakened/stunted, especially under heat/drought stress or poor soil. Optimum disease development at 24-28 degC.
diseases.cultural_control: Rotate with cereal and green-manure crops; soil solarization (25-gauge polythene, 30 days summer); use resistant varieties (Welsh onion lines); late planting reduces incidence; long rotation with non-host crops.
diseases.chemical_control: No fungicide separately dosed for pink root rot
diseases.dosage: Not applicable

diseases.name: Black mould / Green mould (post-harvest)
diseases.scientific_name: Aspergillus niger van Tiegham (black mould); A. fumigatus / A. alliaceus (green mould)
diseases.symptoms: Infection usually enters through neck tissue as foliage dies at maturity; bulbs discolour black (or green) around the neck with shriveling of scales; masses of powdery spores form streaks along veins between outer dry scales, sometimes advancing into fleshy inner scales. Favoured above 30 degC in field or 24 degC in storage with 6+ hours of free surface moisture.
diseases.cultural_control: Field-dry onions for two days after harvest then shade-dry for 10-15 days before storage; store seed/bulb only after proper drying; maintain proper storage aeration; avoid bruising during harvest/storage/transport; store at 1-15 degC.
diseases.chemical_control: No fungicide listed; entirely a post-harvest handling/storage disease per the document
diseases.dosage: Not applicable

diseases.name: Bacterial brown rot / Soft rot / Slippery skin
diseases.scientific_name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa (Schroter) Migula / Pseudomonas allicola Starr and Burk; soft rot: Erwinia carotovora pv. carotovora
diseases.symptoms: Field symptoms show one or two wilted, pale-yellow, dieback leaves in the leaf cluster centre while other leaves stay green; bulb neck tissue softens; internal scales become watery ('cooked'); squeezing the base makes rotted inner tissue slide out through the neck ('slippery skin'). Favoured by moisture and 5-41 degC, heavy irrigation and persistent dew.
diseases.cultural_control: Grow under optimum tilth, fertilizer, drainage and weed-free conditions with crop rotation; proper curing and rapid drying after harvest; discard affected bulbs before storage; artificial curing needed during rainy season.
diseases.chemical_control: No chemical control listed; cultural/curing practices are the primary measure
diseases.dosage: Not applicable

Onion.general_safety_precautions: Section XIII (Basic Precautions in Pesticides Usage) mirrors the standard NIPHM guidance: purchase only required quantities in sealed, approved-label containers with invoice; store away from house premises, food/feed, children/livestock, sunlight/rain, and never store weedicides with other pesticides; never transport pesticides with food; wear gloves, face mask and head covering while preparing spray solution with clean water; use correct, leak-free equipment with proper nozzles (never unclog with mouth); do not spray in hot/windy conditions or just before/after rain; avoid tank-mixing different pesticides; wash equipment after use; dispose of leftover solution and containers away from water sources, crushing and burying containers rather than reusing them. Section XII covers pesticide toxicity classification and poisoning first aid.
Onion.waiting_period_notes: No explicit numeric pre-harvest waiting-period/PHI table is given for individual pesticides on onion. Section X (Safety Measures) instead addresses harvest handling (avoid damaging the protective outer bulb layers) and post-harvest curing (dry bulbs in a dark, dry place at 30-45 degC and 60-75% RH for 1-4 days until necks brown, then store at 35-45 degF/70-75% RH).

Mango.source_title: AESA Based IPM Package for Mango - Directorate of Plant Protection Quarantine and Storage / National Institute of Plant Health Management (NIPHM), Government of India

pests.name: Mango hopper
pests.scientific_name: Idioscopus clypealis, I. nitidulus, I. niveosparsus, Amritodus atkinsoni
pests.symptoms: Wedge-shaped nymphs and adults puncture and suck sap from tender parts, reducing plant vigour and destroying the inflorescence, causing fruit drop; heavy sap draining causes curling/drying of infested tissue; honeydew excretion promotes sooty mould.
pests.cultural_control: Prune dense orchards in December; orchard/field sanitation and rogueing; keep nursery clean of weeds/grasses; remove alternate hosts (hibiscus, custard apple, guava); avoid dense planting, maintain open canopy by pruning overcrowded branches after the rainy season; avoid excess nitrogen; smoke orchards by burning crop residue/cow dung cake in the evening.
pests.biological_control: Apply Metarhizium anisopliae @ 1x10^8 cfu/ml or Beauveria bassiana @ 10^8 cfu/ml on tree trunk once in the off-season and twice at 7-day intervals during flowering; parasitoids Polynema spp., Gonatocerus sp., Tetrastichus sp.; predators Mallada boninensis, Plexippus paykullii.
pests.chemical_control: Buprofezin 25% SC; Imidacloprid 17.8% SL; Lambda-cyhalothrin 5% EC; Dimethoate 30% EC
pests.dosage: Buprofezin 25% SC @ 1.25 ml/L water, 5-15 L per tree; or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 3 ml/L, 10 L/tree; or Lambda-cyhalothrin 5% EC @ 0.5-1.0 ml/L water; or Dimethoate 30% EC @ 990-1320 ml in 600-800 L water/acre

pests.name: Mango mealybug
pests.symptoms: Adult bugs, covered with whitish waxy powder, colonize the bark of the trunk, young shoots and panicles; nymphs ascend and settle on inflorescence causing flower drop and reduced fruit set; honeydew excretion promotes sooty mould development.
pests.cultural_control: Flood the orchard with water in October to kill eggs; plough the orchard in November; rake soil around the tree trunk to expose eggs to natural enemies/sun and remove weeds; fasten alkathene sheet (400 gauge) or grease band (25 cm wide) with mud plastering around the trunk 30 cm above ground in mid-December; destroy infested fallen leaves with scales in July-August.
pests.biological_control: Release 10-15 grubs per tree of the coccinellid predator Cryptolaemus montrouzieri.
pests.chemical_control: Dimethoate 30% EC; Monocrotophos 36% SL (avoid at fruiting stage)
pests.dosage: Dimethoate 30% EC @ 990-1320 ml in 600-800 L water/acre; or Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 600-800 ml in 200-800 L water/acre (do not use Monocrotophos at fruiting stage)

pests.name: Fruit fly
pests.scientific_name: Bactrocera dorsalis Hendel, B. correcta Bezzi, B. zonata Saunders
pests.symptoms: Females puncture the outer wall of mature fruit with the ovipositor and lay eggs in clusters in the mesocarp; hatching maggots feed on fruit pulp, and infested fruits start rotting from secondary infection.
pests.cultural_control: 30-40 days before harvest, collect and dispose of infested/fallen fruits to prevent further multiplication; plough the orchard in November-December to expose pupae to sun's heat.
pests.biological_control: Use methyl eugenol pheromone trap @ 4/acre; parasitoids Fopius arisanus, Diachasmimorpha kraussi.
pests.chemical_control: Deltamethrin bait spray; methyl eugenol + malathion trap mixture
pests.dosage: Bait splash: 100 g jaggery in 1 L water + 1 ml deltamethrin, applied to the trunk once or twice at weekly intervals if infestation is heavy; Male annihilation trap: methyl eugenol 1 ml/L water + 1 ml malathion, 10 ml of mixture per trap at 25 locations/ha; also hot water fruit treatment at 48+-1 degC for 4-5 minutes

pests.name: Inflorescence midge
pests.symptoms: Larvae tunnel the inflorescence axis and destroy it, causing bending and drying of the inflorescence; a second attack at fruit-set has maggots boring into tender fruits which yellow and drop; a third attack targets tender new leaves encircling the inflorescence, with the first (inflorescence) attack the most damaging.
pests.cultural_control: Deep ploughing of the orchard in October-November to expose pupae/diapausing larvae to sun's heat, killing them.
pests.biological_control: Parasitoids Tetrastichus sp., Platygaster sp., Systasis dasyneurae, Aprostocetus spp.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in the crop-stage table beyond cultural ploughing control
pests.dosage: Not applicable - the document lists only cultural control (deep ploughing) for this pest

pests.name: Stem borer
pests.symptoms: Grubs tunnel irregularly in the sapwood of trunk or branches, feeding on vascular tissue and interrupting nutrient/water transport; causes drying of terminal shoots in early stages, frass extrusion and sap oozing from holes, and wilting of branches or the entire tree.
pests.cultural_control: Clean hole and pour kerosene/petrol/crude oil or formalin into the borer hole, then plug the tunnel entrance with cotton wool and seal with mud paste; use light trap @ 1/acre.
pests.biological_control: Not specifically listed for stem borer beyond common biological practices.
pests.chemical_control: Monocrotophos 36% SL
pests.dosage: Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 600-800 ml in 200-800 L water/acre

pests.name: Bark eating caterpillar
pests.symptoms: Caterpillars bore into the trunk or branch junctions and remain hidden in tunnels by day, emerging at night to feed on bark; construct galleries with webbing of wood frass and faecal pellets hanging outside the tunnel; heavy infestation retards tree growth and fruit yield.
pests.cultural_control: Keep the orchard clean and healthy; cut and remove dried branches which harbour the pest.
pests.biological_control: Not specifically listed beyond common cultural/mechanical/biological practices.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in the crop-stage table for this pest
pests.dosage: Not applicable

pests.name: Stone weevil
pests.symptoms: Larvae develop inside the mango stone/seed, damaging the kernel; associated with fallen and infested fruit.
pests.cultural_control: Collect and destroy infested/fallen fruits weekly until harvest; plough the orchard after harvest to expose hibernating adults; destroy all left-over seeds in the orchard and at processing units.
pests.biological_control: Natural enemies recorded include the mite Rhizoglyphus sp., ants (Camponotus sp., Monomorium sp., Oecophylla smaragdina) and the fungus Beauveria bassiana (pathogenic on the weevil).
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in the crop-stage table for this pest
pests.dosage: Not applicable

pests.name: Shoot gall psylla
pests.symptoms: Nymphs induce gall formation on shoots; galls with nymphs are the visible sign of infestation, affecting shoot vigour.
pests.cultural_control: Collect and destroy galls containing nymphs.
pests.biological_control: Conserve predators: black ladybird beetle, purplish pirate bug, brown lacewing, tiny parasitic wasp.
pests.chemical_control: Not separately dosed in the crop-stage table for this pest
pests.dosage: Not applicable

pests.name: Shoot borer
pests.symptoms: Larvae bore into tender shoots; attacked shoots die back and need clipping; associated with drying of terminal growth.
