pests.cultural_control: Clip and destroy attacked shoots; clean the hole and pour kerosene/petrol/crude oil or formalin into the stem-borer hole and plug with cotton wool/mud; use light trap @ 1/acre.
pests.biological_control: Not specifically listed beyond common biological practices.
pests.chemical_control: Monocrotophos 36% SL
pests.dosage: Monocrotophos 36% SL @ 600-800 ml in 200-800 L water/acre

pests.name: Scale insects (regional)
pests.scientific_name: Chloropulvinaria polygonata Cockerell, Aspidiotus destructor Signoret
pests.symptoms: Sap-sucking insects colonizing branches and twigs; heavy infestation weakens plant parts and is often associated with ant attendance.
pests.cultural_control: Prune heavily infested plant parts (branches/twigs), preferably in summer, and destroy them in a pit until natural enemies escape, then burn remaining debris; remove attendant ants to allow natural enemies to work.
pests.biological_control: Removal of attendant ants permits natural enemy activity (predators/parasitoids not separately named for this pest).
pests.chemical_control: Malathion 50% EC
pests.dosage: Malathion 50% EC @ 900-1200 ml in 600-800 L water/acre

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.symptoms: White superficial powdery fungal growth on leaves, panicle stalks, flowers and young fruits; affected flowers/fruits drop prematurely, reducing crop load or preventing fruit set; young leaves show purplish-brown coalesced patches. Favoured by rain/mist with cooler nights during flowering.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid spraying at full bloom; prune diseased leaves and malformed panicles harbouring the pathogen to reduce primary inoculum.
diseases.chemical_control: Azoxystrobin 23% SC; Carbendazim 46.27% SC; Hexaconazole 5% EC; Sulphur 80% WP
diseases.dosage: Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 100 ml (0.1%) per 100 L water depending on tree canopy size; or Carbendazim 46.27% SC @ 0.1% (100 ml/100 L); or Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 0.1% (100 ml/100 L); or Sulphur 80% WP @ 1.25 kg in 300-400 L water/acre

diseases.name: Anthracnose
diseases.scientific_name: Colletotrichum gloeosporioides Stoneman, Spaull and Schrenk
diseases.symptoms: Causes leaf spot, blossom blight, withertip, twig blight and fruit rot; tender shoots/foliage die back; black spots develop on panicles and fruits, severe cases destroying the entire inflorescence; young infected fruit develop black spots, shrivel and drop; fruit infected at maturity carries the fungus into storage. Favoured by high humidity, frequent rain and 24-32 degC.
diseases.cultural_control: Collect and burn diseased leaves, twigs, gall-midge-infected leaves and fruits; cover fruits on the tree with paper bags 15 days before harvest.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified in the document (post-harvest botanical/bio-inoculant dip treatments are mentioned generally for post-harvest disease control).
diseases.chemical_control: Azoxystrobin 23% SC; Copper oxychloride 50% WG
diseases.dosage: Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 100 ml (0.1%) per 100 L water depending on tree canopy; or Copper oxychloride 50% WG @ 0.24% (240 g/100 L water) as required

diseases.name: Die back
diseases.symptoms: Twigs dry back from the top downward, particularly in older trees, followed by leaf drying giving a 'fire scorch' appearance; internal wood browning is seen when split open; cracks appear on branches with gum exudation before dying; graft unions of nursery plants can die when affected. Most conspicuous October-November, favoured by high humidity/moisture.
diseases.cultural_control: Select disease-free scion wood for propagation; take care to prevent introduction of disease in new orchards; prune infected portions with 3 inches of healthy wood removed below the infection site, followed by spraying/pasting with copper oxychloride or cow-dung paste on cut ends.
diseases.chemical_control: Copper oxychloride paste (on pruning cuts)
diseases.dosage: Paste cut ends with copper oxychloride (or cow dung) after pruning infected wood; no foliar spray dose separately specified for die back

diseases.name: Sooty mould
diseases.symptoms: Recognized by a black velvety fungal coating on leaf/twig surfaces, growing on honeydew excreted by mealybug, scale insects and hoppers; in severe cases the whole tree appears black. Favoured by high humidity and moist conditions.
diseases.cultural_control: Prune affected branches and promptly destroy them; control of the underlying honeydew-producing insects (mealybug, scale, hopper) is essential to prevent recurrence.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified in the document (indirect control via biocontrol of the insect vectors).
diseases.chemical_control: No fungicide specifically listed; managed by controlling the causal honeydew-secreting insects
diseases.dosage: Not applicable - control the insect vectors (see Mango hopper, Mango mealybug, Scale insects entries)

diseases.name: Mango malformation complex
diseases.scientific_name: Fusarium mangiferae Wollenweber & Reinking (associated with mite Aceria mangiferae)
diseases.symptoms: Vegetative malformation: young seedlings develop abnormal, swollen growths with very short internodes. Floral malformation: flower buds transform into vegetative buds with many small leaves/stems and reduced internodes, giving a 'witches' broom' appearance; flower buds seldom open and remain dull green.
diseases.cultural_control: Prune and burn floral-malformed panicles/vegetative-malformed shoots to reduce incidence; application of NAA (200 ppm) in the first week of October (before bud differentiation), followed by de-blossoming in late December/January, reduces malformation incidence.
diseases.biological_control: Not specified (mite vector Aceria mangiferae control would reduce wound-associated infection, per the disease description).
diseases.chemical_control: No fungicide specifically dosed; managed via pruning and plant growth regulator (NAA) application
diseases.dosage: NAA @ 200 ppm spray in first week of October, followed by de-blossoming in late December/January

diseases.name: Gummosis
diseases.scientific_name: Lasiodiplodia theobromae (Pat.) Griffon and Maubl. (syn. Botryodiplodia theobromae)
diseases.symptoms: Profuse oozing of gum on the surface of affected wood, trunk bark and larger (especially cracked) branches; in severe cases gum droplets trickle down the stem, bark turns dark brown with longitudinal cracks and rots completely, and the tree dries up from cracking/rotting/girdling. Favoured by warm weather.
diseases.cultural_control: Remove or clean the diseased bark/portion and paste with cow dung paste.
diseases.chemical_control: No fungicide specifically listed; managed by removing diseased bark and pasting the wound
diseases.dosage: Not applicable

diseases.name: Postharvest disease complex (Anthracnose, Stem end rot, Aspergillus/Black mould rot)
diseases.scientific_name: Colletotrichum gloeosporioides (anthracnose); Lasiodiplodia theobromae (stem end rot); Aspergillus niger (black mould rot)
diseases.symptoms: Post-harvest fruit rot symptoms including black anthracnose spots, stem-end rotting and black mould discoloration, developing during storage, transit and marketing, especially in fruit infected at the mature stage in the field.
diseases.cultural_control: Avoid harvesting immature fruit; cool fruit immediately after harvest and store in well-ventilated containers.
diseases.biological_control: Fruits sprayed with a mixture of bio-inoculants; post-harvest botanical fungicide dip treatments can control storage diseases.
diseases.chemical_control: Hot water treatment (physical control, commonly combined with fungicide/bio-inoculant dips)
diseases.dosage: Hot water treatment at 52 degC for 4-5 minutes

diseases.name: Bacterial canker (regional)
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves, leaf stalks, stems, twigs, branches and fruits developing into typical cankers; on leaves, light-yellow angular raised lesions (1-4 mm) enlarge/coalesce into dark-brown necrotic cankerous patches; on fruit, water-soaked dark brown/black lesions grow into raised or flat cankerous spots (1-5 mm) that burst, releasing gummy, highly contagious bacterial ooze. Spring favours disease development.
diseases.cultural_control: Regular orchard inspection, sanitation and seedling certification; use mango stones for rootstock only from healthy fruit; use wind-breaks to reduce wounding that facilitates infection.
diseases.chemical_control: No specific bactericide dosage listed; managed via sanitation and certified planting material
diseases.dosage: Not applicable

diseases.name: Red rust (regional)
diseases.symptoms: Rusty red, greenish-grey velvety circular spots mainly on leaves (also petioles and young twig bark) that turn reddish-brown and coalesce into larger irregular patches; reduces photosynthetic activity and causes defoliation, lowering plant vigour. More common in closely planted orchards; favoured by frequent rain and warm weather, poor nutrition/drainage.
diseases.cultural_control: Maintain plant vigour with balanced nutrition to reduce severity.
diseases.chemical_control: Copper oxychloride
diseases.dosage: Spray copper oxychloride twice during July/August at 15-day intervals, timed with onset of rains

diseases.name: Phoma blight (regional)
diseases.symptoms: Symptoms noticeable mainly on old leaves; angular, minute, irregular, yellow-to-light-brown lesions scattered over the leaf lamina enlarge and change colour from brown to cinnamon becoming irregular, with dark margins and dull-grey necrotic centres; severe infection causes coalescing patches (3.5-13 cm), complete withering and defoliation. Favoured by rainy season.
diseases.cultural_control: Collect and burn affected branches; balanced nutrition provides resistance to phoma blight.
diseases.chemical_control: No fungicide specifically dosed in the crop-stage table for phoma blight
diseases.dosage: Not applicable

diseases.name: Root rot and Damping off (nursery)
diseases.symptoms: Sudden dropping of leaves after seedling emergence; during prolonged rainy/humid weather, circular-to-irregular water-soaked patches occur at/below ground level, enlarging until they girdle the entire seedling base. Favoured by high humidity, high soil moisture, cloudiness and temperatures below 24 degC.
diseases.cultural_control: Well-decomposed FYM coupled with Trichoderma viride/harzianum in nursery beds; raised nursery beds; nursery bed fumigation with 4% formalin.
diseases.biological_control: Trichoderma viride/harzianum incorporated in nursery FYM.
diseases.chemical_control: Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (used for planting-pit drench against soil pests/termites, supporting overall nursery pest/disease management)
diseases.dosage: Drench planting pits with Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 5 ml/L water

Mango.general_safety_precautions: The mango package follows the standard NIPHM safety framework (as in the other AESA-based packages): purchase only required pesticide quantities in sealed, approved-label containers; store away from house premises, food/feed, children/livestock, sunlight/rain, keeping weedicides separate; never transport pesticides with food; wear gloves, face mask and head covering when preparing spray solution; use correct, leak-free spray equipment with proper nozzles; avoid spraying in high wind or just before/after rain; avoid tank-mixing different pesticides; wash equipment after use and dispose of containers by crushing/burying away from water sources.
Mango.waiting_period_notes: No explicit numeric pre-harvest waiting-period/PHI table per pesticide is given for mango. Section XII (Safety Measures) instead covers harvesting precautions (use of clippers or careful twisting, avoiding wet-weather harvest and fruit contact with soil, harvesting in late morning to avoid oil-gland discolouration) and post-harvest handling (hot water treatment at 48 +-1 degC for fruit flies and 52 degC for post-harvest fungal disease control, cool storage) rather than per-chemical waiting days.
